environment.description: Spring Boot 3.1 application deployed on EC2 in a public subnet. Logs are shipped via Fluentd to a centralized Elasticsearch/Kibana stack (ELK) accessible to the SOC team. The Logback configuration uses PatternLayout with no sanitization. The ELK stack renders log fields in Kibana dashboards. An attacker can inject CRLF sequences and fake log entries, or inject JNDI lookup strings targeting Log4Shell (if log4j-core is on classpath via transitive dependency), or craft log entries that exploit downstream log consumers (XSS in Kibana, SIEM rule poisoning). The EC2 instance has a public IP and full internet egress via IGW, allowing JNDI/LDAP callbacks to attacker-controlled servers.

config.runtime: Spring Boot 3.1.2 on Amazon Linux 2023 EC2
config.logging: Logback 1.4.8 with PatternLayout, no OWASP encoder
config.network: VPC public subnet with Internet Gateway, security group allows all outbound
config.dependencies: log4j-core 2.17.0 present as transitive dependency via legacy audit library
